---
title: "CoralNet to Darwin Core"
toc: false
---

::: {.lead}
This website shows how to turn CoralNet files into Darwin Core.

The files come from photoquadrats on a rocky shore.
The survey used the MBON Pole to Pole method.
People and a computer marked the organisms in each photo in CoralNet.

Darwin Core is a common table format for biodiversity data.
OBIS uses Darwin Core for its data archive.
:::

This example is from the Azores in 2026.
It has 207 photos and 20,700 points.
The photos come from four field groups.
The conversion makes 208 events, 504 occurrences, and 2,637 measurements.

## The two scripts

There is one Python script and one R script.
Each one does the whole conversion.
They do not need a config file.
The names and settings are at the top of each script.

The script looks long because it lists every column and every taxon.
The [Steps](steps.qmd) page shows the conversion in order.

Both scripts write the same files.
You only need to run one of them.

::: {.callout-note}
This example covers one survey. It is not a general tool.
To use another survey, change the names and numbers at the top of the script.
Also check the label table in the script.
:::

## What you get

| file | rows | what it is |
|---|---:|---|
| `event.csv` | 208 | one survey event and 207 photo events |
| `occurrence.csv` | 504 | one taxon in one photo |
| `extendedmeasurementorfact.csv` | 2,637 | cover, point counts, and quadrat details |
| `meta.xml` | — | tells the IPT how the columns map to Darwin Core |
| `p2p-azores-2026.zip` | — | all files together, ready for the IPT |

See [Output files](outputs.qmd) for the downloads.
